address: 14870 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065
profile.reading:
This building is SLC6, the fifth and newest data center on DataBank's Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, roughly 20 miles south of Salt Lake City. DataBank's own campus materials place SLC6 at 14870 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 88,250 square feet of IT space and 22 megawatts of critical IT load, the largest single building on the campus, built to an N+1 power design DataBank describes as 100 percent renewable-sourced, with N+1 cooling. A third-party data center aggregator independently corroborates the same 88,250 square foot and 22 megawatt figures and states SLC6 opened in 2023, a year DataBank's own materials describe it as the campus's final and most recently completed building, consistent with that third-party date though DataBank's own page text does not itself spell out the exact year. DataBank acquired the underlying Granite Point site from C7 Data Centers in 2017 and has since built out the campus in phases culminating in SLC6. Across the full five-building campus, DataBank states a combined 257,770 square feet of IT space and roughly 45.9 megawatts of critical IT load on about 23 acres, served by a 66-megawatt substation and diverse A and B feeds from Rocky Mountain Power in an N+1 configuration, with FISMA, SOC 1/2, HIPAA/HITECH, PCI DSS, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 compliance certifications. Utah's "Silicon Slopes" technology corridor has drawn data center, software, and fintech employers to Salt Lake and Utah counties, and Bluffdale's industrial-zoned Pony Express Road corridor has become a recognized regional data center cluster anchored by this campus.

Rocky Mountain Power filed for what it described as Utah's first major large-load energy agreement under the state's 2025 large-load legislation in early February 2026, an "Operation Gigawatt" filing with the Utah Public Service Commission covering a data center customer that agreed to cover its own service costs; this filing does not name DataBank or the Granite Point campus specifically, so it is noted here only as regional grid-planning context, not as a confirmed connection to SLC6. Utah's broader "Silicon Slopes" branding effort has helped position the state as a lower-cost alternative to coastal data center markets for operators seeking reliable power and a business-friendly regulatory climate.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC6, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14870 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 22 MW of critical IT load and 88,250 IT square feet. That same page states SLC6 was the fifth and final data center constructed on this campus, opening in 2023. This row own address was independently used this session to help correct a contradictory address array on a sibling row on the same campus, SLC5, whose prior data had wrongly carried this row own address alongside its correct one.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC6 in Bluffdale, Utah publishes 22 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest publicly disclosed data center in the state by power consumption.

The facility opened in 2023 as the fifth building on Granite Point Campus and spans 88,250 square feet of technical space. At typical colocation densities of 10 kW per rack, this power budget supports roughly 2,200 racks. At the higher densities required for AI training, around 40 kW per rack, the same 22 MW supports approximately 550 racks. These figures reveal how constrained power becomes for compute-dense workloads: quadrupling the power per rack cuts usable density to a quarter.

The operator publishes no details on cooling architecture, power redundancy, or how much capacity is already committed versus available. This gap matters for AI projects seeking unallocated power, since a facility's published megawatts do not indicate headroom for new tenants. Among Utah's 21 mapped data centers, only three publish power figures at all, and those three total 39 MW. Utah's actual installed capacity remains largely invisible in public specifications.
